extracted.intended_audience: school principals and local education administrators writing Title III / ESEA preliminary and formal proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation criteria for planning, drafting, submitting, and justifying a Title III (ESEA) preliminary proposal from a single elementary school, including needs assessment, objectives, timetable, staffing, budget, compliance, dissemination, and evaluation of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity / Funding program understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand the funding source purpose, calendar, required format, and realistic success rates (e.g., 'one-sixth of all submitted proposals obtain funding').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend workshops (e.g., 'Proposal Writers' workshop), obtain the guidebook of the exact format and necessary applications, and note time demands and statistics so the school can commit to competition for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs selection and ranking (Rationale — Needs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank identified school needs to determine proposal effort and focus (the principal convened staff and PTA to identify primary needs and rank them).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use meetings with assistant principals, specialists, and PTA members to surface shortages (e.g., audio-visual materials, cultural experiences, motivation materials, parental involvement) and choose a 'different' approach focused on the highest-priority need(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Needs assessment (evidence-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate the critical local need with data and stakeholder input (reading test scores, teacher consultations, parent discussions, community demographics).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include test score tables, trends over years, qualitative input from teachers and parents, and tie the need to state action goals (e.g., Illinois 'Action Goals for the Seventies').

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear, measurable objectives / outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify concrete, measurable goals for the project (example: 'increase reading by a median gain of ten months').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State target population, measurable gains (median, percentiles), and secondary objectives such as increased parent involvement or humanizing education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal components / required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include all standard elements: abstract, narrative (project description), objectives, timetable, evaluation, staffing, budget, equipment list, dissemination, assurances, and forms (Form A, Form B, Form C etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the guidebook format exactly; provide an abstract, detailed narrative (activities, phases), preliminary budget summary, itemized equipment (items over $50), and required forms/letters (e.g., letter of transmittal, assurances).

rubrics_metrics.name: Writer & team roles and delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: Designate the proposal writer and define roles for school leadership, specialists, PTA representatives, and other staff (the principal served as writer with assistant principals, reading specialists, and PTA involvement).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify responsibilities (e.g., project teacher schedules field trips and develops units; assistant principals assume more management; PTA to handle parent objectives) so execution is feasible within timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Planning process and meetings (strategy for execution)
rubrics_metrics.description: Organize structured planning sessions to pool effort, secure teacher and parent input, refine objectives, and gain proposal support (series of meetings scheduled with clear purposes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Schedule committee meetings timed to allow data collection, objective setting, and proposal evaluation; use contributors' ideas as sounding boards and document agreed-upon goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timetable and strict adherence to deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish and meet the program and local deadlines (example four key dates: workshop, Board deadline, OSPI closing date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efficiency is a prerequisite; delays in approvals can cause missed deadlines; schedule intermediate committee meeting dates to ensure on-time submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval checkpoints / routing
rubrics_metrics.description: Route the proposal through the required approval checkpoints (district superintendent, Area Associate Superintendent and Director of Area Government Programs, Board of Education, then State OSPI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect editorial review and possible requests to redefine concepts or change activities; obtain each approval in sequence and be prepared to revise before proceeding to the next checkpoint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation of proposal success (post-submission criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judge the success of the proposal process by four considerations: (1) approval for submission to OSPI, (2) degree of parent involvement and staff/administrator support, (3) responsiveness to identified student needs, and (4) whether academic growth was worth the effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track approvals, participation metrics, alignment of activities to needs, and cost/benefit in staff time versus student outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation / educational distinctiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Demonstrate an innovative approach that differs from existing methods and addresses motivation and engagement (e.g., using videotaped field trips as a basis for reading instruction).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why the approach is different and necessary for disadvantaged students, and document potential for creative inputs, flexibility, and increased student motivation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project narrative clarity and activity specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a detailed narrative describing participants, activities, phases, and instructional sequence (example: 20 two-week mini-units based on videotaped field trips, with follow-up lessons).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify who does what (project teacher responsibilities, classroom teacher roles, parent involvement), schedule of activities, and how materials (tapes, scripts) will be used for instruction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Target population and area served
rubrics_metrics.description: Define precisely the participant population and geographic scope (example: 200 fourth grade pupils at Van Vlissingen Elementary; share activities with neighboring public and parochial schools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include enrollment numbers, demographic composition, and list of schools/organizations that will be served or invited to participate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Staffing plan: funded and unfunded personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: List staff to be funded by the grant (project teacher, teacher aides, video technician, secretary) and staff not funded but involved (classroom teachers, chaperones), with duties and time allocations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate full-time, part-time, and support roles, and show how existing staff will contribute; describe inservice/training expectations for regular teachers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budgeting, cost justification, and itemization
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare a preliminary budget summary with categories (salaries, contracted services, materials, travel, equipment), grand total, and itemize equipment costing $50.00 or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include salary breakdowns, administrative and instructional equipment amounts, travel and dissemination costs, and provide justification for each cost line; attach additional sheets if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances, legal authority, and compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide signed assurances that the applicant has legal authority, will comply with Civil Rights (Title VI), Public Law requirements, departmental regulations, reporting, and authorized representative documentation (notarized).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach copies of authorizing documents, include a signed statement that all facts are true, and ensure compliance with HEW/Department regulations (45 CFR Part 80) and local/state policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participation and representation in planning
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure participation of persons broadly representative of the cultural and educational resources of the area, including representatives of potential beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document involvement of parents, staff, local councils, and community members in planning and decision-making to satisfy participation assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination plan tailored to audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan dissemination of objectives, methods, and progress to different audiences (community newspapers; parent newsletters; PTA and local school council meetings; district/area/central office reports; local private schools; professional publications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify channels and frequency (e.g., news releases, monthly PTA meetings, quarterly evaluations, invitations to neighboring schools, submission to journals if results are research-worthy).

rubrics_metrics.name: Phase-in, sustainability and continuation strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the project will be phased in, how initial equipment/staffing costs will be reduced over time, and plans for incorporation into regular programs if successful.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain carry-over of equipment, strategies to continue without Title III after evaluation, and how staffing changes might allow long-term adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up strategies if proposal is not funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify next steps in case of non-funding: request OSPI review/hearing and plan to revise and resubmit in a subsequent cycle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the OSPI review privilege for unsuccessful candidates and maintain committee determination to produce a successful proposal in a future year (e.g., 1975-76).

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope control and efficiency (avoid deviation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain focus on the established thrust; pressing timelines can negate some advantages and ideas that deviate from the approved thrust should be set aside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be prepared to postpone attractive but off-thrust ideas to keep the proposal feasible and on schedule for submission.
